contract.direct_answer:
Method (not a result): To resolve a list of gene symbols to verified ENSDARG IDs, each symbol must be looked up in the authoritative identifier resolver — Ensembl Zebrafish (Danio rerio), corroborated by ZFIN for zebrafish-specific nomenclature/synonyms. For every input symbol you either (a) return the single verified ENSDARG the resolver assigns, or (b) if the resolver returns no match (or only an ambiguous/withdrawn match), emit a POSITIVE NOT_FOUND flag for that symbol rather than guessing. I cannot execute the resolution here because the evidence bundle contains only database descriptions and 'Key entities resolved in DI: (none checked)' — no actual symbol→ENSDARG bindings were retrieved. So every symbol in the (unprovided) list is effectively NOT_FOUND pending a live lookup against Ensembl_DanioRerio/ZFIN.

Why IDs must never come from memory: ENSDARG accessions are opaque, versioned, and change over Ensembl releases (genes get merged, split, retired, or re-mapped), and gene symbols are frequently reused, aliased, or reassigned between species. Recalling an ID from memory produces plausible-looking but unverifiable/incorrect bindings (hallucinated accessions), silently corrupting every downstream analysis (interactions, expression, orthology). The only trustworthy binding is one returned by the authoritative resolver at query time — hence memory is prohibited and unresolved symbols must be surfaced as positive NOT_FOUND rather than filled in.</parameter>
